title.narrative: Anhui Aged Care System Demonstration Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Anhui Aged Care System Demonstration Project for China is to support the government of Anhui in developing and managing a diversified, three-tiered aged care service delivery system for the elderly, particularly those with limited functional ability.It has four components. First component, supporting the development of government stewardship capacity will support development of a unified information system to facilitate both the development and management of the aged care service system; design and pilot an assessment of functional ability and needs to improve the effectiveness and quality of care services; establish a set of quality standards for aged care services; and support training and building a professional workforce (managers and administrators) for aged care services; Second component, strengthening community-based and home-based care services will strengthen the delivery and management of community-based and home-based care services in two project cities. The funds will be used to finance civil works, goods, consulting services and capacity-building activities and will contribute to the services improvements envisaged by the authorities; Third component, strengthening the delivery and management of nursing care will strengthen the delivery and management of urban skilled nursing facilities in two project cities; increase the capacity of government-run urban welfare homes in one project city; and strengthen the delivery and management capacity of government-run rural welfare homes, including developing options for public-private partnership in one district and four counties of one project municipality; Fourth component, project management, monitoring, and evaluation will support project management and build capacity in general management and planning to ensure an effective and efficient project implementation; provide technical guidance through a project expert panel (PEP) to support project implementation; and support the monitoring of the implementation of project activities and the achievements of the intended results.

The project development objective (PDO) is to support the government of Anhui province in developing and managing a diversified, three-tiered aged care service delivery system for the elderly, particularly those with limited functional ability.

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator 3.2 Occupancy rates of beds at the project sites (Percentage)

comment.narrative: Achieved overall (54% against revised 52% target). Mixed results across sub-tiers. The aggregate bed occupancy rate of 54% at closing met the final revised target of 52%, representing a meaningful improvement from the 39% baseline. Results varied significantly across facility types. The aggregate target was reduced in both restructurings (from 78% to 64% to 52%) principally to reflect: (i) the phased commissioning timeline of new facilities, which compressed the period available to build up occupancy before project close; (ii) the shift in the facility mix toward rural welfare homes (with inherently different resident recruitment dynamics than urban institutions); and (iii) the facility-specific completion delays at Anqing and Suzhou that reduced the effective commissioned bed stock available for occupation.

comment.narrative: Achieved — exceeded (719% of the final revised target; 0.6% of original target). At completion, 107,804 users were recorded across the three deployed prefectures (Anqing, Lu'an, and Suzhou), exceeding the final revised target of 15,000. However, performance against the original target of 18,255,678 — which had assumed province-wide deployment to all sixteen prefectures — remained below expectations. This gap reflects a compounding set of constraints: a protracted procurement process for the system integration contract, the technical complexity of multi-department data integration and cleaning across legacy systems, and limited technical and organizational capacity at the prefecture level to absorb the rollout within the project timeline. Post-closing expansion to additional prefectures was formally documented as an active rollout trajectory, underscoring that the deployment shortfall represents a timing and capacity constraint rather than an absence of demand or system functionality

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator 2.1 Number of newly constructed/upgraded community service stations at the project sites

comment.narrative: Substantially achieved (99% of the final revised target). 110 community service stations were delivered at project closing, representing 99% of the final revised target of 111. Performance against the original target of 158 (70% reached) reflects a series of scope revisions driven by site eligibility and financing shifts. At the 1st restructuring (2023), the target was reduced from 158 to 131 due to: (i) ineligibility of 30 planned Anqing stations (unresolved land ownership, incomplete demolition, or insufficient physical space), offset by identification of 19 new compliant sites; (ii) relocation of 14 Lu'an sites; and (iii) the reallocation of USD 7.84 million in loan proceeds from Component 2 to Component 3 to fund the expansion of rural welfare home upgrades. At the 2nd restructuring (2025), the target was further reduced to 111, principally driven by a partial loan cancellation of USD 15.1 million under Component 2. This cancellation itself reflected a financing substitution.

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator 1.3 Number of aged care service standards developed at the provincial levels and financed by the project

comment.narrative: Achieved (100% of the final revised target; 129% of original target). All 62 aged care service standards were developed and completed at project closing, meeting the revised target exactly and exceeding the original target of 48 by 29%. The target was increased from 48 to 62 at the 1st restructuring (2023), reflecting the expanded scope of the provincial standards program: the actual pipeline of standards under development — driven by regulatory needs identified during implementation — proved broader than originally planned, covering functional ability assessment protocols, emergency rescue center setup requirements, elderly information collection systems, home care service file management, and mental care service standards, in addition to the core institutional care standards envisaged at appraisal.

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator 1.1 Number of modules developed and operating for the provincial information system (Number)

comment.narrative: Achieved (100% of the final revised target; 175% of original target). All seven functional modules of the Provincial Aged Care Information System were completed and operationalized by project closing, exceeding the original target of 4 modules. The target was increased from 4 to 7 at the 1st restructuring (2023), reflecting a deliberate expansion of the system's design scope: the full conceptual architecture, which had been elaborated during detailed design, encompassed seven modules — (i) public service and beneficiary portal, (ii) facility management, (iii) government supervision and monitoring, (iv) functional ability and needs assessment management, (v) financial management and subsidy disbursement, (vi) AI-based safety monitoring across nursing facilities, and (vii) data analytics and reporting.

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator 1.4 Number of aged care professionals participating in training activities

comment.narrative: Achieved (100% of both the aggregate and women's sub-target). The indicator was met at project closing: 9,402 aged care professionals participated in project-financed training activities, meeting the revised target of 9,402. Professional training under this IRI covered a broad range of occupational categories — including caregivers, nurses, physicians, facility operators, service providers, managers, and government officials — reflecting the project's intent to build capacity across the full staffing spectrum of the aged care sector, not only at the managerial level (which is separately tracked under PDO Indicator 4). The original target of 9,795 was revised slightly downward to 9,402 at the 1st restructuring (2023), reflecting COVID-19 impacts on in-person training modalities and a recalibration of the achievable training cohort.

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator 1.5 Proportion of the elderly benefiting from the project who received functional ability/needs assessments

comment.narrative: Achieved — exceeded (130% of the final revised target). The indicator substantially exceeded its final revised target: 90% of eligible elderly at project sites received a standardized functional ability and needs assessment, against a revised target of 69%. This result marks a decisive shift from supply-driven to needs-based service allocation — a central objective of the project's stewardship dimension. The original target of 92% was revised downward to 69% at the 1st restructuring (2023), reflecting a methodological refinement introduced after the mid-term review that distinguished project-financed assessments (using the standardized provincial toolkit developed under Component 1) from those conducted through parallel provincial programs not financed by the project. The revised 69% target therefore reflects a more conservative and verifiable definition, and the 90% outcome at closing represents a genuine achievement against a tighter measurement standard.

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator 3.1. Number of newly constructed or upgraded nursing care beds at the project sites

comment.narrative: Partially achieved (71% of the final revised target). Additional beds expected within one year of project close. At completion, 4,423 nursing care beds had been newly constructed or upgraded across project sites, representing 71% of the final revised target of 6,193. The shortfall is attributable to two specific facilities — the Anqing First People's Hospital nursing home and certain Suzhou rural welfare home facilities — where the construction of the physical structures was substantially complete by project closing but bed furnishings, medical equipment, and internal fit-out had not yet been installed. These facilities were functional as buildings but not yet fully commissioned as care beds. Based on government project completion report, total commissioned beds has reached 6,244 by March 30, 2026, surpassing the revised target.

title.narrative: Percentage of dedicated public outlays for elderly care spent on purchasing aged care services from non-public providers in urban areas in the project sites (Percentage, arithmetic average)

comment.narrative: Achieved (100% of the final revised target). The indicator was met exactly at project closing and has remained at or above 22.4% consistently since 2021, ranging between 22.4% and 23.3% across annual reporting periods. This performance represents a structural and durable shift in how Anhui's provincial and municipal governments finance aged care services — from direct public provision to contracted delivery through qualified private and non-government providers. The original target of 27% was revised downward to 22.4% at the 1st restructuring (2023) to reflect COVID-19-era fiscal constraints, during which public spending priorities shifted toward direct infrastructure investment and safety enhancement at aged care facilities, temporarily reducing the relative share available for contracted services. The 22.4% target was retained at the 2nd restructuring (2025).

title.narrative: Share of aged care service providers who meet the requirements of construction and service standards at the project sites (Percentage)

comment.narrative: Achieved (100% of the final revised target). The indicator was met exactly at project closing, rising from a 34% baseline to 93.7% — a near-threefold improvement representing a fundamental transformation in the quality compliance landscape of Anhui's aged care sector. The original 98% target was revised downward to 93.7% at the 1st restructuring (2023) to reflect Anhui's 2021 introduction of a new five-level accreditation system that combined both infrastructure compliance and service delivery performance standards into a single unified assessment — a substantially more demanding benchmark than the narrower, infrastructure-only compliance standard that had been assumed at appraisal. The actual achievement of 93.7% against this higher standard therefore understates the improvement relative to the original compliance regime.

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator 4.1. Satisfaction of consumers and their families with aged care services
Intermediate Result Indicator 4.1. Satisfaction of consumers and their families with aged care services

comment.narrative: Achieved — exceeded (overall 106% of target; women 107% of target). Overall consumer satisfaction reached 90.2% (against an 85% target). This indicator and its end targets were introduced at the 1st restructuring (2023); no satisfaction indicator had been included at appraisal. The 2023 mid-term beneficiary satisfaction survey established the baseline values (72% overall, 73% women). The 85% end target was designed to represent a meaningful improvement over the baseline, consistent with project investments in service quality, standards enforcement, and physical facility upgrading. The target and gender sub-target were retained unchanged at the 2nd restructuring (2025). High satisfaction levels were observed across all three care tiers, with consistent positive feedback on responsiveness of service staff, cleanliness and safety of facilities, quality of meals, and the accessibility of digital service channels.
